definitions.definition: A structural similarity between two different systems that allows insights from one to apply to the other.
definitions.example: A map of a subway system is isomorphic to the actual tunnels—the structure is the same even though the map is not the real thing.

definitions.definition: The study of how diseases spread through populations and what controls their spread.
definitions.example: Epidemiology helped us understand how COVID-19 moved from person to person and how to stop it.

definitions.definition: The study of sin—what it is, where it comes from, and how it affects people.
definitions.example: Hamartiology asks questions like 'Why do people do wrong things?' and 'How does sin spread?'

definitions.definition: The average number of new cases one infected person will cause in a completely susceptible population.
definitions.example: If R₀ is 3, each sick person will infect about 3 others, and the disease spreads quickly.

definitions.definition: A mathematical model that divides a population into three groups: Susceptible, Infected, and Recovered, to predict how a disease spreads.
definitions.example: The SIR model can show how many people will get the flu if no one is vaccinated.

definitions.definition: When enough people in a community are immune to a disease that it cannot spread easily, protecting even those who are not immune.
definitions.example: If 95% of kids are vaccinated against measles, the other 5% are still protected because the disease can't find enough hosts.

definitions.definition: Individuals who infect far more people than average, often causing large outbreaks.
definitions.example: One person at a crowded indoor event can infect dozens of others, becoming a super-spreader.

definitions.definition: Separating people who have been exposed to a disease from others to prevent further spread.
definitions.example: If you were near someone with COVID-19, you might be asked to quarantine for 14 days.

definitions.definition: Finding everyone who has been in close contact with an infected person and monitoring them for symptoms.
definitions.example: Health workers call people who sat near a sick passenger on a bus to check if they get sick.

definitions.definition: Giving a person a weakened or dead form of a germ to train their immune system to fight it without getting sick.
definitions.example: Getting a flu shot helps your body recognize and fight the flu virus if you encounter it later.

definitions.definition: Graphs that show the number of new cases of a disease over time, often rising quickly and then falling.
definitions.example: An epidemic curve for a flu outbreak might show a sharp peak in December and a drop in January.

definitions.definition: The spread of a disease or a behavior from one person to another through contact or imitation.
definitions.example: Yawning is a form of contagion—when one person yawns, others often do too.

definitions.definition: A small amount of yeast that spreads through dough and makes it rise; used in the Bible as a metaphor for how a small amount of sin can affect a whole community.
definitions.example: Just as a little yeast makes a whole batch of bread rise, a little sin can influence an entire group.

definitions.definition: A deep, hidden resentment or unforgiveness that grows and causes trouble for many people.
definitions.example: If one person holds a grudge and gossips, it can spread and make a whole group unhappy.

definitions.definition: A person who is not immune to a disease and can become infected.
definitions.example: If you have never had chickenpox and are not vaccinated, you are susceptible to catching it.

definitions.definition: Growing extremely fast because each new case causes more than one additional case.
definitions.example: If you double a penny every day, after 30 days you have over 5 million dollars—that's exponential growth.

definitions.definition: Actions taken to stop a disease or problem from spreading further.
definitions.example: Putting a lid on a pot of boiling water is containment—it keeps the water from splashing everywhere.

definitions.definition: Abandoning or rejecting one's religious faith or beliefs.
definitions.example: If someone who was a Christian decides they no longer believe in God, that is apostasy.

definitions.definition: Being set apart for God, morally pure, and dedicated to living a righteous life.
definitions.example: A person who tries to live without lying, cheating, or hurting others is pursuing holiness.

definitions.definition: The process of learning from and following a teacher, especially in the Christian faith, to grow in spiritual maturity.
definitions.example: A new Christian meets weekly with a mentor to study the Bible and learn how to live faithfully.

definitions.definition: A pattern where a small number of causes produce most of the effects, like 20% of people doing 80% of the work.
definitions.example: In many companies, 20% of the employees do 80% of the important work.

definitions.definition: People who are infected with a disease but show no symptoms, yet can still spread it to others.
definitions.example: Someone with COVID-19 might feel fine but still cough on others and pass the virus.

definitions.definition: Weakened so that it no longer causes disease but still triggers an immune response.
definitions.example: The polio vaccine uses an attenuated virus that is too weak to make you sick but still trains your body to fight polio.

definitions.definition: The ability to judge well, especially to tell right from wrong or good from bad.
definitions.example: A wise person uses discernment to decide whether a friend's advice is helpful or harmful.

definitions.definition: A period of renewed spiritual interest, growth, and commitment in a community or church.
definitions.example: During a revival, many people start praying, reading the Bible, and helping others more than before.

definitions.definition: Equations that describe how a quantity changes over time, often used to model real-world processes like disease spread.
definitions.example: A differential equation can tell you how fast a population of rabbits grows based on how many rabbits there are and how much food is available.

definitions.definition: A structural similarity between two different systems that allows insights from one to apply to the other.
definitions.example: A map of a subway system is isomorphic to the actual tunnels—the structure is the same even though the map is not the real thing.

definitions.definition: A pair of differential equations that model how predator and prey populations change over time.
definitions.example: If there are many rabbits, the fox population grows; then the foxes eat many rabbits, so the rabbit population drops.

definitions.definition: The process of becoming more holy and more like Jesus Christ through the work of the Holy Spirit.
definitions.example: A Christian who prays, reads the Bible, and tries to be kind is growing in sanctification.

definitions.definition: The idea that a scientific theory must be able to be proven wrong by some possible observation or experiment.
definitions.example: The claim 'all swans are white' can be falsified by finding one black swan.

definitions.definition: Research that follows the same group of people over a long period of time to see how they change.
definitions.example: A study that tracks the health of 1,000 people for 20 years to see who develops heart disease is a longitudinal study.

definitions.definition: A population that has never been exposed to a particular germ and therefore has no immunity to it.
definitions.example: When Europeans first arrived in the Americas, Native Americans were immunologically naive to smallpox and died in huge numbers.

definitions.definition: A statement that is accepted as true without proof, used as a starting point for further reasoning.
definitions.example: In geometry, 'a straight line is the shortest distance between two points' is an axiom.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; in simple terms, things tend to become more messy over time.
definitions.example: Your bedroom gets messier on its own, but it takes work to clean it up—that's entropy increasing.

definitions.definition: The study of salvation—how people are saved from sin and its consequences.
definitions.example: Soteriology asks questions like 'How does Jesus save us?' and 'What does it mean to be saved?'
